action_items: Update server.py:949 email subject from 'GigBlast — test email' to 'HCOB Network — test email' (one-character spec miss; no functional impact).
critical_code_review_comments: Security fix is solid: server.py register endpoint (line 297-298) hardcodes role='worker' regardless of payload.role. The UserCreate model still keeps role: Optional[Literal['worker','admin']] for back-compat with old clients — consider dropping the field from the public Pydantic model so the OpenAPI surface no longer advertises an 'admin' option (it currently advertises a flag that is silently ignored, which is confusing for API consumers).

Seed admin logic (server.py:996-1023) only seeds the env-configured admin; the legacy admin@gigblast.com works only because the previous deploy already inserted it. A fresh DB would lose the legacy admin. If back-compat must survive a DB wipe, add an explicit secondary seed for admin@gigblast.com / GigBlast2026!.

APP_NAME env default in server.py:46 still falls back to 'gigblast' if the env var is missing — fine because .env now sets 'hcob', but the default should also be updated to keep storage paths consistent on misconfigured deployments.
Branding string mismatch (server.py:949 'GigBlast — test email') — flagged above; trivial fix.
server.py is still 1031 lines and growing — same modularization comment from iter-2/3 remains open.

rca of the issue: N/A — no production bugs reproduced. The previously-failing iter-1 test (test_register_admin_role expected role=admin to succeed) was a pre-existing security regression: public /api/auth/register honored client-supplied role, allowing privilege escalation. Mitigation already applied by main agent at server.py:297-298 (hardcoded role='worker' in insert payload). New regression test test_register_admin_role_is_silently_downgraded_to_worker proves it: response.role and /auth/me.role both come back as 'worker' even when the request body contains role='admin'.
